strings.name: Elaine Thompson-Herah
strings.summary: Thompson-Herah won both 100 m and 200 m at Rio and Tokyo, adding a relay gold with Jamaica. Her 10.54-second 100 m in 2021 became a major benchmark in women's sprinting. An unexceptional school competitor, she improved after entering Jamaica's University of Technology and MVP club. An Achilles injury ruled her out of Paris; she returned to competition in 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Consecutive Olympic sprint doubles gave her international competitive influence in women's athletics.

strings.highlights.h2.title: 10.54-second 100 m
strings.highlights.h2.text: Set her personal best of 10.54 seconds in Eugene in 2021.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Return after injury
strings.timeline.t1.text: Returned to major competition and helped Jamaica win the women's 4×100 m at World Relays.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Missed Paris through injury
strings.timeline.t2.text: An Achilles injury prevented her Olympic participation.

strings.timeline.t3.text: Won 100 m and 200 m in Birmingham.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Personal best in Eugene
strings.timeline.t4.text: Ran 10.54 in the Diamond League 100 m.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Three Tokyo golds
strings.timeline.t5.text: Retained 100 m and 200 m titles and won 4×100 m with Jamaica.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Rio Olympic double
strings.timeline.t6.text: Won 100 m and 200 m gold at the same Games.
strings.timeline.t7.title: World individual medal
strings.timeline.t7.text: Won 200 m silver in Beijing and relay gold with Jamaica.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Regional relay title
strings.timeline.t8.text: Helped Jamaica win the Central American and Caribbean 4×100 m title.
